question: Why is health care waste management considered a vital component of nursing practice?

options.A: It reduces the financial overhead of hospital administration
options.B: It protects patients, health workers, and the community from infections
options.C: It is primarily a duty assigned exclusively to hospital environmental officers
options.D: It eliminates the need for standard personal protective equipment

explanation: Proper waste management protects patients, staff, and the community from disease transmission and environmental hazards. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T16#GNS122_U3_T16_h1)

question: What role do nurses play in health care waste management due to their profession?

options.A: They are central to generation, sorting, and disposal because they spend the most time at the bedside
options.B: They are only responsible for signing off on external waste transport manifests
options.C: They are legally prohibited from handling any form of clinical refuse
options.D: They act solely as supervisors without any direct handling responsibilities

explanation: Nurses are central to waste management because they form the largest group of professionals and handle waste directly at the bedside. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T16#GNS122_U3_T16_h1)

question: Which of the following best describes non-hazardous health care waste?

options.A: Expired cytotoxic medications and chemical reagents
options.B: Used surgical scalpels and hypodermic needles
options.C: Domestic-type refuse like paper and food remnants posing no special biological risk
options.D: Human anatomical tissues and pathological specimens

explanation: Non-hazardous waste consists of general, domestic-type refuse that can be handled similarly to municipal waste. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T16#GNS122_U3_T16_h2)

question: What color-coded container is typically designated for infectious health care waste in standardized facilities?

options.C: Clear plastic bags with recycling marks
options.D: Blue cardboard boxes with no symbols

explanation: Infectious health care waste is typically segregated into yellow bins marked with biohazard symbols. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T16#GNS122_U3_T16_h2)

question: Which Nigerian agency is specifically involved in environmental standards and regulations enforcement relevant to waste management?
explanation: NESREA stands for the National Environmental Standards and Regulations Enforcement Agency, which enforces environmental standards in Nigeria. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T16#GNS122_U3_T16_h3)

question: What is a primary objective of international frameworks like the Basel Convention regarding health care waste?

options.A: To maximize the export of medical waste to developing countries
options.B: To control transboundary movements of hazardous wastes and protect human health and ecosystems
options.C: To eliminate the need for local waste management policies
options.D: To replace all incineration plants with open burning pits

explanation: The Basel Convention focuses on controlling transboundary movements of hazardous wastes and ensuring their safe disposal to protect health and ecosystems. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T16#GNS122_U3_T16_h3)

question: What does the 'cradle-to-grave' principle dictate regarding health care waste?

options.A: Waste management only matters during the birth and death stages of patient care
options.B: The waste generator remains legally responsible for the waste from its production until final disposal
options.C: Waste can be handed over to any municipal worker without documentation
options.D: Manufacturing companies are responsible for hospital waste once it leaves the ward

explanation: The cradle-to-grave principle holds the waste generator accountable for the waste throughout its entire lifecycle until ultimate safe disposal. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T16#GNS122_U3_T16_h4)

question: What is a potential consequence for a health facility or nurse engaging in illegal dumping of clinical waste?

options.B: Regulatory sanctions, civil litigation, or loss of licensure
options.D: Mandatory transfer to administrative duties only

explanation: Improper waste disposal can lead to severe regulatory penalties, lawsuits, and disciplinary actions affecting professional licensure. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T16#GNS122_U3_T16_h4)

question: When and where should health care waste segregation take place?

options.A: In the hospital incinerator yard at the end of the day
options.B: Immediately at the point of generation
options.C: In the municipal landfill by sanitation workers
options.D: Inside the central storage room after mixing all waste

explanation: Segregation must occur immediately at the point of generation to prevent cross-contamination and reduce handling risks. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T16#GNS122_U3_T16_h5)

question: What safety rule applies to used hypodermic needles after an injection?

options.A: They should be carefully recapped using both hands before disposal
options.B: They should be bent to fit more items into the safety box
options.C: They must never be recapped and should be dropped directly into a puncture-resistant box
options.D: They can be thrown into general waste if the needle is small

explanation: Needles should never be recapped to avoid needle-stick injuries and must be dropped directly into a safety box. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T16#GNS122_U3_T16_h5)

question: What is the primary function of an autoclave in health care waste treatment?

options.A: To burn anatomical waste into fine ash
options.B: To utilize high-pressure steam to sterilize infectious waste and sharps
options.C: To compress general waste into municipal landfills
options.D: To chemically dissolve expired pharmaceutical drugs

explanation: Autoclaves use high-pressure steam to render infectious waste and sharps biologically inactive and safe. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T16#GNS122_U3_T16_h6)

question: Why is proper ward-level waste sorting critical for downstream treatment methods?

options.A: It ensures that incorrect waste does not compromise treatment technologies like autoclaves or incinerators
options.B: It reduces the weight of waste so transport vehicles drive faster
options.C: It eliminates the need for any regional transportation
options.D: It allows hazardous waste to be sold as recycled material

explanation: Correct sorting ensures that specific waste streams go to appropriate treatment facilities without causing operational or safety failures. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T16#GNS122_U3_T16_h6)

question: What is a primary occupational hazard associated with improperly managed health care sharps?

options.A: Chronic respiratory allergies from paper dust
options.B: Percutaneous injuries leading to blood-borne pathogen exposure
options.D: Musculoskeletal strain from lifting light general waste

explanation: Improperly managed sharps frequently cause needle-stick or percutaneous injuries, exposing workers to infections like HIV and Hepatitis. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T16#GNS122_U3_T16_h7)

question: What immediate medical intervention should be accessible to a nurse following an accidental needle-stick injury?

options.C: Mandatory suspension from clinical practice for six months
options.D: Surgical debridement of the affected digit

explanation: Access to post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) is critical following needle-stick injuries to mitigate the risk of acquiring infections. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T16#GNS122_U3_T16_h7)

question: Why are nurses uniquely positioned to drive waste management policy implementation?

options.A: They control the national budget for environmental health agencies
options.B: They are front-line coordinators who oversee ward workflows and mentor staff
options.C: They are legally mandated to perform all waste incineration themselves
options.D: They have exclusive authority to penalize external waste contractors

explanation: Nurses coordinate patient care and ward workflows, placing them in an ideal leadership position to guide compliance and mentor others. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T16#GNS122_U3_T16_h8)

question: What is an example of an advocacy role a nurse can take regarding institutional waste management?

options.A: Participating in infection control committees to advocate for adequate safety supplies and practical policies
options.B: Ignoring supply shortages to encourage staff resilience
options.C: Recommending the cessation of all waste audits to save time
options.D: Delegating all infection control responsibilities exclusively to patients

explanation: Nurses advocate for safety by participating on committees to secure necessary resources and shape practical hospital policies. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T16#GNS122_U3_T16_h8)
